name: roll_save
description: Roll a saving throw: d20 against the character's Physical, Evasion, Mental, or Luck save, succeeding on a roll equal to or above the score. Call it when an effect threatens the character and the rules allow a save. A failure is recorded; apply what it costs yourself.

character.description: The name of the character making the save.

save.description: Which save: save_physical for bodily harm, save_evasion for dodging, save_mental for willpower, save_luck for blind chance.

cause.description: What the save is against, in a few words.

name: player_roll_save
description: Ask the player to roll a saving throw for their own character, then record the d20 they rolled against the character's Physical, Evasion, Mental, or Luck save. Use it instead of roll_save for the player character: the player presses the roll button and the result is final. A failure is recorded; apply what it costs yourself.

player_input.details: {save} save against {cause}: roll 1d20 and meet or beat your save score.

character.description: The name of the player character making the save.

save.description: Which save: physical for bodily harm, evasion for dodging, mental for willpower, luck for blind chance.

cause.description: What the save is against, in a few words.

prompt.description: What the player is asked to roll, such as 'Roll a Physical save against the poison.'

name: roll_reaction
description: Roll 2d6 for the first reaction of an NPC or group the party meets, adding the greeting character's Charisma modifier when a player character can greet them. The higher the total, the friendlier the reaction. Use it whenever the party meets a creature or group unless bloodshed is certain, and describe the mood to the players before they act.

character.description: The player character greeting the NPC, for the Charisma modifier. Any player character if none greets them.

greeting.description: Whether a player character is in a position to greet the targets, which adds their Charisma modifier.

cause.description: Who or what the party has met.

name: instinct_check
description: Check an NPC's Instinct: roll 1d10 against the Instinct score printed in its statblock. A roll no higher than the score means the creature acts on impulse rather than its best judgment. Player characters never check Instinct.

name.description: The name of the NPC whose instincts are tested.

instinct.description: The creature's Instinct score from its statblock.

cause.description: What tempts the creature to act on impulse.

name: roll_tables
description: Roll on one or more of the rule set's dice tables and log every result. Use the world-generation tables (significant_terrain, terrain_quirk, terrain_antagonists, nation_disputes_with_neighbor, ruler_class, government_struggle, history_event, community_tags, court_tags, ruin_tags, wilderness_tags) to build the starting region. Also available: site_type, site_feature, site_hazard, site_enigma, site_treasure, deeps_type, ruin_characteristic, ruin_encounter_human, ruin_encounter_beast, ruin_encounter_sapient, encounter_template, wilderness_event, dungeon_event, monster_shape, monster_drive, and monster_twist. Use dungeon_reaction (2d6) for a quick reaction, or roll_reaction to add Charisma. The engine returns the results; you decide what they mean.

tables.description: The ids of the tables to roll on, in order. Each is rolled once.

name: travel
description: Travel overland by the WWN rules. A day is ten hours of marching; base speed is 3 mph on plains, 2 in light forest or desert, 1.5 in dense forest or rugged hills, 1 in swamp, and 0.5 in mountains or broken highland. A road doubles the pace, foul weather halves it, and deep snow reduces it to a tenth. The engine moves the character and advances the clock. Apply the returned food, water, firewood, and privation figures with use_item, add_strain, and the usual bookkeeping; foraging takes half a day and a Wis/Survive check at the returned difficulty.

character.description: The player character making the journey.

destination.description: The place the party travels to.

terrain.description: The hardest terrain on the route.

road.description: True when the route follows a road, which doubles the pace.

weather.description: Foul weather halves the pace; deep snow reduces it to a tenth.

days.description: Whole days of travel, from 1 to 30. Defaults to 1.

travelers.description: How many people are travelling, for supply needs. Defaults to 1.

reason.description: A short note on the journey, for the log.

name: roll_initiative
description: Roll initiative for each side of the encounter: 1d8 plus the best Dexterity modifier in the side, with ties going to the party. Call it once the participants have joined the encounter and before the first round. No player character makes an individual initiative roll.

name: start_encounter
description: Start an encounter on a map. Create the map first if the place has none. Add the participants, then call roll_initiative before anyone acts.

map.description: The name of the encounter map where the fight happens.

name: end_encounter
description: End the encounter in progress once the fight, chase, or parley is over.

name: add_participant
description: Add a character to the encounter on a side. Player characters default to the party and NPCs to the foes.

name.description: The name of the character joining the encounter.

side.description: The side they fight on, such as party or foes. Leave it out for the usual side.

name: remove_participant
description: Take a character out of the encounter, such as one who flees or is left behind.

name.description: The name of the character leaving the encounter.

name: attack
description: Make an NPC's attack: d20 plus its attack bonus against the target's Armor Class, with a natural 1 always missing and a natural 20 always hitting. The engine rolls the damage; on a miss it still applies the attack's Shock when the target's AC is low enough. An attack is refused unless the attacker is the character taking their turn, so the player presses Start for the NPC's turn first; pass force true only for an action the story needs outside the turn order, such as an ambush.

attacker.description: The name of the NPC attacking.

attack.description: The name of one of its attacks, as the statblock lists it.

target.description: The name of the character being attacked.

hit_modifier.description: A situational bonus or penalty to the hit roll: -2 long range, -4 firing while meleed or attacking prone, -1 dual wielding, -2 or -4 cover, -2 for total defence.

count.description: How many attacks to resolve. Leave it out to use the statblock's attacks per action, or set 1 for a single attack.

force.description: Resolve the attack even though this is not the attacker's turn. Set it only when the story needs an action outside the turn order, such as an ambush that catches the party unawares.

name: player_attack
description: Ask the player to roll their attack with a carried weapon or unarmed, then record the d20. The engine adds the weapon skill, the best weapon attribute, the attack bonus, and a Warrior's Killing Blow, rolls damage, and applies Shock on a miss when the target's AC is low enough. Use it for the player character; the player presses the roll button and the result is final. An attack is refused unless the player character is taking their turn; their turn starts automatically when it comes up. Pass force true only for an action the story needs outside the turn order.

player_input.details: {weapon} against {target}: roll 1d20 and add your attack bonus. The engine rolls damage.

target.description: The name of the character being attacked.

weapon.description: The carried weapon's name, as given, or unarmed.

hit_modifier.description: A situational bonus or penalty to the hit roll: -2 long range, -4 firing while meleed or attacking prone, -1 dual wielding, -2 or -4 cover, -2 for total defence.

range_band.description: The range band the shot is fired at. Short has no penalty; long gives -2 to hit.

dual_wield.description: True when attacking with two one-handed melee weapons. The engine applies the rule set's dual-wield hit penalty and damage bonus.

force.description: Resolve the attack even though this is not the player character's turn. Set it only when the story needs an action outside the turn order.

prompt.description: What the player is asked to roll, such as 'Roll your attack with the long sword.'

name: resolve_attacks
description: Resolve several NPC attacks on one character at once, such as a creature's several attacks per action or several foes striking the same target. Each attack rolls its own attack die and applies its own damage in turn. Every attacker must be taking their turn unless force is true.

target.description: The name of the character being attacked.

attacks.description: The attacks to resolve, one entry per attack.

force.description: Resolve the attacks even though they are not the attackers' turns. Set it only when the story needs an action outside the turn order, such as an ambush.

name: set_armor
description: Set a character's total Armor Class for a special adjustment or a monster's printed AC. For tracked equipment the adjustment persists as equipment or other defense changes. Use equip_armor for equipment changes.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

name: harm_character
description: Harm a character outside combat, from a fall, poison, exposure, or privation. Use harm from an attack only through attack or player_attack. A PC brought to 0 HP is mortally wounded; an NPC is dead.

stat.description: The stat harmed. Outside combat, usually hp.

name: heal_character
description: Restore lost points of a stat, usually hit points, from a healing spell, art, or item. It never restores more than the character has lost. Recovering a mortally wounded character is a separate act.

amount.description: How many points the healing restores before the cap.

stat.description: The stat to restore. Defaults to hp.

cause.description: What did the healing, such as a spell or art.

name: stabilize
description: Stop a mortally wounded character's dying clock. The character wakes with 1 hit point after ten minutes and gains the Frail condition. In the book this needs an Int/Heal or Dex/Heal check at difficulty 8 plus the rounds since they fell; call roll_check first and stabilize only on a success.

explanation.description: How they were stabilized, such as a tourniquet or a healer's care.

name: recover_character
description: Clear a mortally wounded character's dying state as magical healing does, leaving the harm they took for heal_character to restore. Use it after the character is stabilized and the healing magic reaches them.

name: player_save
description: Pass the player's own d20 roll for a save the engine has marked due after harm. Use it only when a save is owed.

name: retreat
description: Take a character out of the fight. Set safe to true only when the character has a clear route away.

name: rest
description: Record one party rest. Every player character recovers: a night restores hit points equal to their level, one point of System Strain, all spell castings, and scene and day Effort. A few moments restores scene Effort only. A week of bed rest restores all hit points and Strain and ends Frail. The rest moves the clock once. Frail characters recover no hit points or Strain from a single night.

length.description: moments for a short break, night for a full night's rest, extended for a week of bed rest.

interrupted.description: True when something breaks the rest, which then counts as moments only.

name: advance_time
description: Move the campaign clock forward. Use it for downtime, travel you track yourself, or the hour a mortally wounded character has left to live.

name: hire_hireling
description: Hire a retainer into a player character's company. The retainer has a rolled sheet like an NPC's and is controlled by the player. Its wage is paid in silver from the employer each new day, and an employer who cannot pay is reported as unpaid. Leave personality, accent, or quirks out to have them rolled. Names must be unique among locations and characters.

employer.description: The player character paying the wage.

wage.description: Silver per day, zero or more.

name: dismiss_hireling
description: Remove a retainer from its employer's company. It stays where it is and becomes an ordinary NPC.

cause.description: Why the retainer leaves, in a few words.

name: give_item
description: Give a character an item they are given, find, or loot, with no payment. A catalogue item takes its listed size, uses, and damage; a new item needs its size and, for a weapon, its damage dice. Never use it because the player says the character has something or reaches for it: check the inventory first, and if the character does not carry it, say so and let them find, buy, or do without it. Never use it for something the character pays for; use buy_item.

size.description: How much of the inventory it fills. Leave it out for a catalogue item.

damage.description: The weapon's damage dice, such as 1d8. Leave it out for gear.

name: drop_item
description: Remove an item from a character's inventory. Dropping equipped armor or a wielded shield also unequips it and recalculates Armor Class.

name: ready_item
description: Ready a carried item for use, or stow it. A character can keep only half their Strength in slots readied; readied weapons can attack. Readying armor or a shield does not equip it; use equip_armor to wear or wield it. Stowing equipped defense also unequips it. Retrieving a stowed item takes a Main action.

ready.description: True to ready it, false to stow it.

name: equip_armor
description: Wear or remove a carried, readied suit of armor, or wield or stop wielding a carried, readied shield. Only one suit and one shield can be equipped; equipping another replaces that slot. Armor Class and shield protection against Shock update automatically. The returned Armor Class is authoritative: wearing armor or wielding a shield can lower it when a feature such as the Vowed's Unarmored Defense works only without that equipment. Consult the character's features before explaining a change.

item.description: The carried armor or shield's catalogue name.

equipped.description: True to wear or wield it, false to remove it.

name: start_project
description: Begin a long-running effort and track its points toward a target: a personal project, a piece of research, a magic working, or another long effort. The kind and goal are free text; the target is how many points of work it needs. Advance it with advance_project as time, money, and rolls are spent. Use add_faction_asset and take_faction_turn for factions instead.

name.description: The project's name, unique among projects.

kind.description: What sort of effort it is, such as project, research, working, or faction.

target.description: How many progress points it needs.

force.description: Set true to replace a project of the same name.

name: advance_project
description: Add progress to a project, research effort, magic working, or another long effort. Record in the note what the time, money, or roll bought. The project completes when progress reaches its target.

name: abandon_project
description: Give up a project, research effort, magic working, or another long effort.

name: list_projects
description: List every project, research effort, and magic working with its progress, notes, and whether it is complete or abandoned.

name: add_faction_asset
description: Give a faction one of the rule set's assets, such as Infantry, Smugglers, or Farmers. The kind may be the asset's id or its book name. Its cost, hit points, Magic, Attack, Counter, and qualities are resolved from the rule set. An asset can act once per faction turn.

kind.description: The asset kind's id or book name, such as infantry or Infantry.

name.description: A display name for this copy of the asset, unique within the faction. Defaults to the book name.

notes.description: An optional note, such as where the asset is based.

name: update_faction_asset
description: Change a faction asset's display name, qualities, or notes. A note is appended to the asset's record. Use damage_faction_asset and repair_faction_asset for hit points.

asset.description: The asset's name or id within the faction.

notes.description: A note to append to the asset's record.

qualities.description: The asset's full quality list, such as ["Subtle", "Special"].

name: remove_faction_asset
description: Remove or destroy one of a faction's assets.

asset.description: The asset's name or id within the faction.

name: faction_asset_acted
description: Record that a faction asset used its action for the current faction turn. An asset can act only once per turn; the tool refuses a second action. End the turn with take_faction_turn to ready every asset again.

asset.description: The asset's name or id within the faction.

note.description: What the asset did, such as attacking, moving, or repairing.

name: damage_faction_asset
description: Reduce a faction asset's hit points by an amount. Hit points stop at zero rather than going negative.

asset.description: The asset's name or id within the faction.

name: repair_faction_asset
description: Restore a faction asset's hit points by an amount. Hit points stop at the asset's maximum.

asset.description: The asset's name or id within the faction.

name: take_faction_turn
description: Close a faction's current turn and begin the next one. Every asset is ready to act again. Use this after resolving the faction's actions, upkeep, and asset abilities.

note.description: What the faction accomplished this turn.

name: buy_item
description: Buy an object a character keeps, with silver. A catalogue item costs its listed price; for anything else, give both a price and the item's size. Use buy_service for a room, meal, passage, toll, or other service that is not carried. Armor updates the buyer's Armor Class automatically.

price.description: The price in silver for an item not in the catalogue.

size.description: The size of an item not in the catalogue; required for anything the catalogue does not list. Catalogue items keep their listed size.

name: buy_service
description: Buy a service for one or more characters: a room, meal, passage, toll, bribe, or anything else that is not carried away. A listed service uses its listed price and effect, so leave price out. For any other service, give a price you set from similar services. The first character named pays for the whole service. A service never adds an inventory item.

names.description: The characters the service is for. The first one pays.

service.description: The service, such as a room, meal, passage, or toll. Use a listed service's id or name as search_marketplace shows it.

price.description: The price in silver for a service the marketplace does not list. Leave it out for a listed service.

name: search_marketplace
description: Find items and services the marketplace sells, by name or category.

name: create_monster
description: Create a creature from the bestiary and place it at a location. Give the template id (use search_monster to find it) and any changes to its stats, armor, or attacks.

rules.description: Rule ids attached to the creature, whose text the GM sees while it is present.

name: search_monster
description: Find bestiary statblocks by name or description.

name: learn_art
description: Spend an art pick on an art of the character's own tradition. Class charts grant art picks at levels 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 for a full mage, and at levels 2, 3, 6, and 9 for a partial mage (3, 6, and 9 for a partial Necromancer or Elementalist).

art.description: The feature id of the art.

name: improve_attribute
description: Spend skill points on a permanent +1 to one attribute. The first boost costs 1 point, the second 2, and so on to 5, at minimum character levels 2, 2, 3, 6, and 9; a character may buy five in total.

name: roll_starting_silver
description: Give a character starting money instead of an equipment package: roll 3d6 and multiply by 10 silver pieces, as the book allows. Use it once at creation and do not also grant a package.

name: create_encounter_map
description: Make a square grid map for an encounter at a location, such as a ford, room, or yard. A map is needed before start_encounter can be used.

template.description: An optional encounter map template id.

palette.description: A map palette id from map_options: parchment, stone, forest, sea, ember, frost, shadow, or royal.

ambient.description: An ambient look id from map_options: day, dusk, night, torchlit, foggy, underwater, or magical.

background_color.description: A hex colour for the board's ground.

grid_color.description: A hex colour for the board's grid lines.

name: update_encounter_map
description: Change an encounter map's name, location, description, size, look, or extend it on any side. Extending keeps every mark and token, shifting them by the cells added to the left or top.

palette.description: A map palette id from map_options. Leave out to keep it.

ambient.description: An ambient look id from map_options. Leave out to keep it.

background.description: A terrain id for the board's background. Leave out to keep it.

background_color.description: A hex colour for the board's ground. Leave out to keep it.

grid_color.description: A hex colour for the board's grid lines. Leave out to keep it.

extend_left.description: Add columns on the left; existing marks and tokens shift right.

extend_up.description: Add rows at the top; existing marks and tokens shift down.

name: delete_encounter_map
description: Delete an encounter map that is no longer needed.

name: place_participant
description: Put an encounter participant on a cell of the map grid.
